title: Point-blowup domination of an H-projective modification over a regular trait surface
statement: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $F$, residue field $k$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C\to T$ be an integral H-projective scheme with nonempty integral generic fibre [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-kun-projective, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $r:Z\to C$ be H-projective and an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Assume $Z$ is integral, regular and Noetherian (locally Noetherian and quasi-compact), all its local rings have dimension at most two, and every closed point of $Z_k$ has local dimension two [def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $\Gamma$ be integral and $p:\Gamma\to C$ H-projective, also an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Then there are $m\geq0$, a tower $Y=Z_m\xrightarrow{b_m}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}Z_0=Z$, in which each $b_{i+1}$ is the blowup of a reduced closed point $z_i$ of the special fibre $(Z_i)_k$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and a morphism $a:Y\to\Gamma$ with $pa=h$, where $h=r b_1\cdots b_m:Y\to C$. Every $Z_i$ is integral, regular, Noetherian and H-projective over $T$, and every $\mathcal O_{Z_i,z_i}$ is a regular local ring of dimension two. The morphism $h$ is H-projective and an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}F$. Length zero is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0C5H (lemma-extend-rational-map-blowing-up), applied to the rational map Z_F = C_F = Gamma_F from Z to Gamma over C, i.e. the existing node lem-sfb-surface-rational-map-point-resolution with S=C, X=Z, Y=Gamma, U=Z_F; with Tag 0AGR (lemma-blowup-regular) for the local dimension of later centres and H-projectivity of point blowups over the affine trait. Agent-formulated trait application carrying returned Steps 4--6 (graph, 0BFP, 0AHI are inside 0C5H). Supporting de Jong Lemma 3.13 proof, printed p.609 (primary PDF read online; archival PDF WANTED).

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $A$. Its maximal ideal is nonzero and principal by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and $A$ is Noetherian since every ideal is principal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power], every nonzero denominator is a unit times a power of $\pi$, so $A[1/\pi]=F$. The same formula shows that every nonzero prime contains $\pi$ and hence is the maximal ideal. Thus $T$ has precisely the generic point and the closed point. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}F=D(\pi)$ is open in $T$. Its inverse image $U=Z_F$ is the corresponding open subscheme, by [def-pc-base-change]; it is nonempty since $Z_F\cong C_F$. Since $Z$ is integral, its nonempty open $U$ is dense [def-pc-integral-scheme].

By [lem-trf-h-projective-composition], $Z\to C\to T$ is H-projective, hence proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Its image is closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism] and contains the generic point, so it is all of $T$. In particular $Z_k$ is nonempty; by [def-pc-scheme-fibre] it is the closed subspace of $Z$ over the closed point. Choose a minimal nonempty closed subset $D$ of $Z$ contained in $Z_k$, using [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. For each $d\in D$, minimality gives $\overline{\{d\}}=D$. This makes $D$ irreducible, and uniqueness in [lem-sc-scheme-sober] implies $D$ is a singleton. Its point is closed in $Z_k$ and $Z$, so its local ring has dimension two by hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 01WE (lemma-H-projective-composition), 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper); properties.tex Tag 01OZ and schemes.tex Tag 01IS for the closed-point argument.

proof.text: The chain formula [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] identify chains of generalizations starting at a point with chains of irreducible closed subsets starting at its closure. Taking the supremum over all starting points therefore gives $\dim Z=\sup_{z\in Z}\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, with topological dimension defined in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The assumed upper bound on every local dimension and the dimension-two point found in step 2 give $\dim Z=2$.

source.place: Tag 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring); the preceding dimension lemma proof identifies dimension with the supremum of local-ring dimensions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] to $p:\Gamma\to C$. On $U=Z_F$, define $f$ as $Z_F\xrightarrow{r_F}C_F\xrightarrow{p_F^{-1}}\Gamma_F\to\Gamma$. Its composite with $p$ is $r|_U$, by the inverse identity for $p_F$ and the base-change triangles [def-pc-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-surface-rational-map-point-resolution] with $S=C$, $X=Z$, $Y=\Gamma$, the structure maps $r,p$, and this dense open $U$. Its hypotheses hold by steps 1--3 and the assumed integrality, regularity and Noetherianity of $Z$. It gives a tower $Z_m\to\cdots\to Z_0=Z$ and a $C$-morphism $a:Z_m\to\Gamma$. Every level is integral, regular and Noetherian; each centre is a reduced closed point outside the inverse image of $U$; the tower composite $b:Z_m\to Z$ is an isomorphism over $U$.

source.place: Tag 0C5H (lemma-extend-rational-map-blowing-up), applied over C, not merely over the trait.

proof.text: Let $q_i:Z_i\to T$ be the structure morphism obtained by composing the tower with $Z\to T$. By [def-pc-base-change], the inverse image of $U=Z_F$ in $Z_i$ is $(Z_i)_F$. Its complement is $(Z_i)_k$ on underlying spaces, because $T$ has just the two points of step 1 [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Hence every centre furnished in step 4 belongs to the special fibre.

source.place: Tag 0C5H, centres outside the original rational-map domain; scheme-theoretic fibre convention, schemes.tex Tags 01K0 and 01K1.

proof.text: Induct on $i$ to prove that every closed point of $(Z_i)_k$ has local dimension two. This is assumed for $i=0$. Regularity of each level was obtained in step 4, so the next centre has a regular local ring of dimension two [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-geometry] to this centre. For a closed point $x\in(Z_{i+1})_k$, its singleton is closed in $Z_{i+1}$ since the special fibre is closed. Properness of $b_{i+1}$ makes its image a closed point of $(Z_i)_k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]. If the image is the centre, the geometry lemma gives local dimension two. Otherwise its off-centre isomorphism identifies the local ring at $x$ with the dimension-two local ring given by induction. This proves the invariant and the required dimension of every centre. For $m=0$ there are no centres to check.

source.place: Tags 0AGR (lemma-blowup-regular) and 0AGQ (lemma-blowup), global form in the cited geometry node.

proof.text: For each centre the defining ideal sheaf is quasi-coherent by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. On an affine chart of the Noetherian level $Z_i$, its ideal is finitely generated: the chart ring is Noetherian by [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth], and this is exactly [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Thus the ideal sheaf is of finite type. Starting with the H-projective map $Z\to T$ of step 2, apply [lem-sfb-projective-affine-base-blowup] at each stage, over the affine Noetherian base $T$. It gives both H-projectivity of $b_{i+1}$ and H-projectivity of $Z_{i+1}\to T$. This induction proves the asserted H-projectivity at every level.

source.place: Tag 02NS (lemma-blowing-up-projective); morphisms.tex Tags 087S and 01WE as packaged by the existing affine-base blowup node.

proof.text: Put $Y=Z_m$ and $h=r\circ b$. The fact that $a$ is a $C$-morphism means exactly $p\circ a=h$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Every $b_i$ and $r$ is H-projective, so [lem-trf-h-projective-composition] shows $h$ is H-projective. Its generic restriction is the composite of the isomorphism $b_F$ from step 4 and the assumed isomorphism $r_F$, so it is an isomorphism. The intermediate scheme properties were supplied by step 4, their H-projectivity by step 7, and the centre properties by steps 5--6. All these constructions allow $m=0$, in which case $b$ is the identity and $h=r$.

proof_origin.place: Trait application of Tag 0C5H, with Tags 0AGR, 02IZ, 02NS, 087S and 01WE; written-out dimension and projectivity bookkeeping.
